name: Oregonator: a stiff chemical oscillator
description:
The Oregonator, Field and Noyes's three-variable model of the Belousov–Zhabotinsky reaction, in the scaled form of the stiff test problem OREGO: y1 is bromous acid, y2 bromide and y3 the cerium catalyst, and each is a compartment with its dy/dt term from that problem. The concentrations swing across five decades, y1 from 1 up to 1.2·10⁵ and back in every cycle, so the value axis is logarithmic. At t = 360 the run is within 4·10⁻⁵ of the problem's reference solution (1.000815, 1228.18, 132.055).

The parameters span seven orders of magnitude and the problem is stiff throughout: the NDF solver crosses the 360 seconds in 1654 steps, dp45 in 3.4 million.
